description: The line plot illustrates the relationship between the number of child nodes (tree width) and the Accuracy@1 (%) for two large vision-language models, GPT-4o and Claude-3.5-Sonnet, on a task involving geometric problems (Geomverse). The x-axis, labeled "Num. of Child Nodes (Tree Width)", ranges from 1 to 7, representing the breadth of the search tree. The y-axis, labeled "Accuracy@1 (%)", measures the model's performance and is scaled from 15 to 35. Two distinct lines represent the models: GPT-4o (blue, with circular markers) and Claude-3.5-Sonnet (light blue, with 'x' markers). The GPT-4o model's accuracy increases from 24.4% at a tree width of 1 to a peak of 34.4% at a tree width of 5, before decreasing to 31.1% at a tree width of 7. In contrast, the Claude-3.5-Sonnet model shows a peak accuracy of 27.8% at a tree width of 3, followed by a steady decline to 20.0% at a tree width of 7. The plot clearly demonstrates an inverted U-shaped trend for both models, indicating that performance improves with increased tree width up to a point, after which it declines.
